content: Trichinella spiralis is a parasitic nematode that infects rats, pigs, and humans, causing the disease trichinosis. It is often referred to as the pork worm because it is commonly found in undercooked pork products. The adult worms are small and mature in the intestines of intermediate hosts, such as pigs. Female worms produce live larvae, which penetrate the intestinal wall and enter the bloodstream and lymphatic system. These larvae are then transported to striated muscle tissue, where they encyst, meaning they become enclosed in a protective capsule. Encysted larvae in muscle tissue can remain viable for extended periods. When humans consume infected muscle tissue, the cysts are digested in the stomach, releasing the larvae. These larvae migrate to the intestines, where they mature and begin a new life cycle. Female worms live for approximately six weeks and release larvae during this time. The migration and encystment of larvae can lead to symptoms such as fever, muscle pain, and, in severe cases, death due to their ability to damage living tissue. A hallmark of Trichinella spiralis infection is the presence of splinter hemorrhages (small, linear bleeding under the nails) and periorbital edema (swelling around the eyes). Trichinella spiralis belongs to the phylum Nematoda. Treatment Antimicrobial Regimen: 1. Preferred Treatment Option 1: Albendazole, 400 mg taken orally twice daily for 8 to 14 days. 2. Preferred Treatment Option 2: Mebendazole, 200-400 mg taken orally three times daily for 3 days, followed by 400-500 mg taken orally three times daily for 10 days. Important Notes: Both Albendazole and Mebendazole regimens are appropriate for both adults and children. These medications are contraindicated during pregnancy and are not recommended for children under the age of 2 years. Alternative Regimens: 1. For severe symptoms, Prednisone (a corticosteroid) can be administered at a dosage of 30-60 mg per day for 10-15 days. 2. Pyrantel can be used as an alternative, with a dosage of 10-20 mg/kg as a single dose for 2-3 days.
